items.title: Harold Dejan Interview, 1963-03-29
items.q: I can't think of the name of it, by Professor Pritchard Howard.

ctx.x: Well, how does the brass band play that's different from jazz playing?

Well, most of the brass bands, they play a watching tempo to walk, and like people are, when you're playing a brass band, you play maybe a six-eighth or two-fourth tempo, like some people call it split time, but it's two-fourth or six-eighth. Four-fourth, too. Yeah, they call it four-fourth, but they play it in two-fourth time. If they play a number, four-fourth number, they're going to play it in two-fourth time, but instead of saying two-fourth, they call it split time. That's what they call it, but it end up…
Has Perrier the music changed in your auction during the last thirty years?
